target.title: feat(claude): show Max usage multiplier (5x/20x) in plan label
target.body:
## Summary

- Surface the Claude Max usage multiplier in the plan label — `default_claude_max_5x` / `default_claude_max_20x` now read **"Claude Max 5x" / "Claude Max 20x"** instead of a flattened "Max".
- Append the multiplier only when the rate-limit tier string names the resolved plan, so a mismatched subscription type never inherits a stray multiplier.
- Leave Pro / Team / Enterprise labels unchanged; mirrors the existing Codex Pro 5x/20x treatment (#882).
- Update the `docs/claude.md` plan-inference note and add a CHANGELOG entry.

## Root cause

Anthropic encodes the Max tier in the rate-limit tier string (`default_claude_max_5x`, `default_claude_max_20x`), but `ClaudePlan.fromRateLimitTier` matched on `.contains("max")` and discarded the rest, so every Max subscription rendered as a flat "Max". A new `usageMultiplier(for:rateLimitTier:)` extracts a `[0-9]+x` suffix and `brandedLoginMethod(rateLimitTier:)` appends it, wired through the OAuth and web label entry points.

Tier strings: every value this change keys on already appears in the repo's own fixtures — `default_claude_max_20x`, `claude_pro`, `claude_team`, `claude_enterprise`, `claude_max` across `ClaudeUsageTests` / `ClaudePlanResolverTests` / `ClaudeOAuthTests`; `default_claude_max_5x` I also confirmed live on a real account. Those fixtures already mix `default_claude_*` and short `claude_*` forms, so extraction is substring-based and tier-agnostic — it stays correct across that prefix variance, and a future `default_claude_team_5x` would render "Claude Team 5x" automatically.

## Proof (live before / after)

Same real Max 5x account (`oauthAccount.organizationRateLimitTier = "default_claude_max_5x"`), same command, minutes apart, macOS 26.5.1. No email or org identity appears in the output.

Before — installed v0.40.0 release CLI (pre-change):

```console
$ codexbar usage --provider claude --source oauth --no-color
== Claude (oauth) ==
Session: 100% left [============]
Resets 9:00 PM
Weekly: 69% left [========----]
Pace: 26% in reserve | Expected 57% used | Lasts until reset
Resets Jul 9 at 5:00 PM
Plan: Claude Max
```

After — this branch (`swift build --product CodexBarCLI`, head `888121c5`):

```console
$ .build/debug/CodexBarCLI usage --provider claude --source oauth --no-color
== Claude (oauth) ==
Session: 100% left [============]
Resets 8:59 PM
Weekly: 69% left [========----]
Pace: 26% in reserve | Expected 57% used | Lasts until reset
Resets Jul 9 at 4:59 PM
Plan: Claude Max 5X
```

Note: the CLI's pre-existing `plan.capitalized` rendering (`CLIRenderer.swift:422`, untouched here) displays the label's "5x" as "5X" in terminal output; the raw label and the menu UI carry "Claude Max 5x".

## Validation

- `swift test --filter ClaudePlanResolverTests` — 7 tests passed (5x/20x, bare Max, mismatched team + max_5x, web path).
- `swift test --filter ClaudeUsageTests` — 39 tests passed.
- `make check` — SwiftFormat, SwiftLint, repository checks passed (0 violations).
- `make test` — full 48-shard local suite passed.
- Live OAuth fetch from this branch on a real Max 5x account renders the new label (proof above).

## Risk

Low and contained to the Claude plan label string. The multiplier is appended only when the tier names the resolved plan, so Pro/Team/Enterprise output is unchanged and a mismatched subscription type cannot leak a "5x"/"20x". Downstream consumers that re-parse the label (`fromCompatibilityLoginMethod`) still resolve "Claude Max 5x" to `.max`, so history bucketing and subscription detection are unaffected.
